# SafeUnfollow (safeunfollow.app)

> SafeUnfollow is a web app at safeunfollow.app that reads the official Instagram data export in your browser and shows who unfollowed you, who does not follow back, and who is mutual.
> The analysis is free at any export size, and the full export file is an optional purchase.
> You pick the export from your own device, and it is never sent to a server.
> SafeUnfollow never asks for your Instagram login.
> Nothing SafeUnfollow publishes acts inside your Instagram account. SafeUnfollow does not publish a browser extension.
> SafeUnfollow.app is not affiliated with safeunfollow.com or with any browser extension named SafeUnfollow.

## Facts

- Reads the official Instagram data export, requested from the Meta Accounts Center, in JSON or HTML (both since 2026-08-29).
- Shows unfollowers, non-mutuals, mutuals, pending requests, restricted and close-friends accounts, with the follow date the export recorded (since 2026-10-25).
- Tested on a synthetic export of 1,000,000 accounts: about 21 seconds from choosing the file to results, in desktop Chrome (November 2026). One desktop run; no phone has been tested at that size.
- Available in 10 languages.
- Open source under the MIT licence, archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22663615

## What it costs

- The analysis is free in full: every badge, every filter, every account, at any export size.
- Exporting the result as a readable report, CSV or JSON is a one-time licence key, priced by country. A free sample report (every count, the first 10 accounts) downloads before anything is asked for.
- Some pages on safeunfollow.app show Google ads, and the site runs analytics (a self-hosted Umami and Google Analytics). The privacy policy names each one. Our code never passes your export to any of them.

## Documentation

- [Documentation index](https://safeunfollow.app/docs): every page below, from requesting the export to reading the result.
- [How to download your Instagram data as a ZIP](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/instagram-export): the export request, the settings that matter, and how long Meta takes.
- [User guide](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/user-guide): picking the export, badges, filtering, search.
- [FAQ](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/faq): what it does and does not do.
- [Is the unfollowers tracker legit?](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/is-it-safe): why no login is asked for and what that rules out.
- [Troubleshooting](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/troubleshooting): upload failures and what causes them.
- [Technical specification](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/tech-spec): storage, parsing and the client-side architecture.
- [Privacy](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/privacy): what is processed where.
- [Accessibility](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/accessibility): keyboard, screen reader and RTL support.
- [Alternatives compared](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/compare): how it differs from trackers that ask for a login.
- [SafeUnfollow vs followsback.com](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/compare/vs-followsback): both read the official export; what differs is the account-size limit, the billing period and whether the client is open source, with their figures dated on the page.
- [SafeUnfollow vs Unfollowgram](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/compare/vs-unfollowgram): for a reader looking for Unfollowgram; it states no features or prices for it.
- [SafeUnfollow vs Followers App](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/compare/vs-followers-app): "Followers App" names several products, so this compares only how a tracker gets your data.
- [Roadmap](https://safeunfollow.app/docs/roadmap): what is built and what is planned.

## Start here

- [Open the app](https://safeunfollow.app/)
- [Pick your export](https://safeunfollow.app/upload)

## Completeness

This file lists every page the documentation sources declare, and a test fails the build if one
is missing. A page left out on purpose would be named below on its own bullet, as a path with its
reason, so an omission is a recorded decision. Nothing is currently excluded.
